haiku-low.q1: Connection returns, app comes to foreground, and every 60 seconds while online.
haiku-low.q3: The server detects it by comparing the change's base version with the note's current server version; a mismatch is a conflict.
haiku-low.q4: n1 holds the first arriving phone's text at v4. The second phone's body is saved as new note n2 titled "T (conflict)" at v1.
haiku-low.q5: One change holding the latest full body, keeping the original base_version and change_id.
haiku-low.q6: Each change has a change_id; the server checks its applied-changes table first and returns the stored result without reapplying.
haiku-low.q7: On the phone, as the last applied seq (cursor). It is updated in the same local transaction that applies each downloaded page.
haiku-low.q8: The partial response applies nothing and the cursor stays put, so the next sync refetches from the same cursor.
haiku-low.q9: The conflict outcome in the ack tells it (with the conflict note id). It resets the displayed note to the server copy; the conflict note arrives on download.
haiku-low.q10: Only after an ack from the server, whether accepted or conflict.
haiku-low.q11: Only the server copy is updated, not the displayed draft. The queued change will then conflict, which is correct.
haiku-low.q12: The edit becomes a separate pending outbox row, uploaded later, rather than joining the sent change.

sonnet.q1: When the connection returns, when the app comes to the foreground, and every 60 seconds while online. Only one sync runs at a time; triggers during a running sync are skipped.
sonnet.q3: The server. It compares the change's base version with the note's current server version; a mismatch is a conflict.
sonnet.q4: The first to arrive wins: the note holds the first phone's text at version +1 (e.g. v4). The second phone's body is stored as a new note titled "<original title> (conflict)" at version 1, with its id derived from change_id. Both are in the change log, and the outcomes are recorded in the applied-changes table.
sonnet.q5: One change per note: a single outbox row with the original change_id, the original base_version, and the latest full body (full body, no diffs).
sonnet.q6: Each change carries a change_id (UUID). The server looks it up in the applied-changes table in the same transaction; if found, it returns the stored result and applies nothing. Otherwise it applies the change and stores the outcome. The phone resends the same change_ids.
sonnet.q7: In the phone's cursor (the last seq applied). It is updated in the same local transaction that upserts a downloaded page, set to the page's next_cursor.
sonnet.q8: A partial response applies nothing and the cursor stays unchanged. The same request is retried (refetched) from the unchanged cursor, so nothing is skipped or applied twice.
sonnet.q9: It learns from the conflict outcome in the upload response (ack). It resets the displayed note to its last known server copy (server_title/server_body). The user's text arrives as the conflict note on download.
sonnet.q10: Only after the server acks it, whether the outcome is accepted or conflict. A failed upload or lost response leaves the row queued.
sonnet.q11: Only the stored server copy of the note is updated, not the displayed draft. The queued change will then conflict, which the document calls correct.
sonnet.q12: The edit becomes a separate pending outbox row. When the ack arrives, its base version is filled in from the ack, or from the conflict outcome if the upload lost.
